content.title: About
content.content: Beef is the meat of cattle, obtained from various parts of the carcass. Round steak comes from the rear section of the animal and is a lean cut with a mild flavor and moderate fat. It is commonly grilled, pan‑seared, or roasted to retain juiciness and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The round cut is located in the hindquarter and is one of the leanest beef cuts.
Beef is a rich source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.
Historically, round steak has been used in high‑cuisine dishes such as steak tartare and beef carpaccio.
Meat quality depends heavily on cattle breed, rearing conditions, and aging process.
In some regions the round is also called “top‑blade” or “bottom round.”

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef provides all essential amino acids needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Heme iron from beef helps prevent anemia, especially in women and children.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals boost immunity and aid wound healing.

items.title: Creatine
items.content: Natural creatine in beef enhances muscular energy metabolism, beneficial for athletes.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked beef can harbor pathogens such as E. coli and Salmonella.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef proteins.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: High amounts can exacerbate gout symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Round steak is best cooked to medium‑rare (55‑60 °C) to keep it tender. Marinate in olive oil with herbs, sear on a hot pan, or grill. Slice thinly and serve with vegetables, sauces, or in salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh beef in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic film or in an airtight container. For longer storage freeze at –18 °C using vacuum‑sealed bags. Thaw frozen beef in the fridge, not at room temperature, before cooking.
